##  · K5-q-units — R12 charging unit: timebase ticks rather than whole microseconds

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Charging in timebase ticks, min 1 tick per deschedule, runtime capped at 2^40 ticks (2^40 x STRIDE 2^20 fits in u64); timeouts and deadlines stay in µs. Added: carry the per-budget division remainder, because weight is up to u32 (KERNEL-SPEC budget table) and STRIDE is 2^20 (libs/sys/src/lib.rs:139), so large weights would otherwise be charged 0 for short bursts. The model carries the remainder, with a mutation. Goes into the K5 KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit; the owner confirms at plan approval.

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `12b5c1028061ce65260f73cabcf33e17` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12: "pass += runtime x STRIDE / weight". The spec's time unit is µs. If the kernel measures runtime in whole µs, a thread that runs under 1 µs per burst and blocks is charged 0. That's a sub-µs gaming channel; a syscall round trip on real hardware can be under 1 µs.
> 
> Recommendation: charge runtime in `time` ticks (the timebase), with a minimum of 1 tick per deschedule and the runtime capped at 2^40 ticks so the u64 step can't overflow. The step is ticks x STRIDE / weight. Weights are relative, so shares are unchanged; only the resolution improves. Timeouts and deadlines stay in µs as the ABI says.
> 
> The model keeps µs. Its differential test with the kernel's stride crate runs in one unit, and a model mutation R12ShortRunsFree shows the gaming would be caught.
> 
> Ask: approve ticks for charging, or require µs with carried remainders.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `9c72158b41b9cf6e368db80405fc27b6` · 2026-09-24T17:54:19Z

> Approved: charge in timebase ticks, a minimum of 1 tick per deschedule, runtime capped at 2^40 ticks (2^40 x STRIDE 2^20 = 2^60 fits in u64). Timeouts and deadlines stay in µs per the ABI. One more hole, the same gaming channel one level down: weight is a u32 (up to 2^32) and STRIDE is 2^20, so ticks x STRIDE / weight floors to 0 for any weight above 2^20 x ticks. A large-weight budget (init, the steward, drivers, which get large manifest weights) running 1 tick and blocking is charged nothing. Fix it exactly: carry the division remainder per budget (rem = (rem + ticks x STRIDE) mod weight, step = the quotient), so charging is exact over time and never free. A floor of step >= 1 would overcharge large weights. Put the remainder in the overflow section (rem < weight <= u32 max, so the sum fits). Model: keep µs if its differential test against the kernel's stride crate runs in one unit, but the model must carry the remainder too. Extend R12ShortRunsFree, or add R12DropRemainder, and show that a large-weight short-burst spinner is caught. Add this to the K5 KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit: R12 charges in ticks with an exact remainder.

### Orchestrator · Resolved

Added: carry the per-budget division remainder, because weight is up to u32 (KERNEL-SPEC budget table) and STRIDE is 2^20 (libs/sys/src/lib.rs:139), so large weights would otherwise be charged 0 for short bursts. The model carries the remainder, with a mutation. Goes into the K5 KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit; the owner confirms at plan approval.
